messages:
acme-admin: Hey team — after our IdP session refresh this morning several users (including me) suddenly lose all project role visibility in the console. When switching orgs we get a 403 "permission denied" and the UI shows no roles. Happening for ~8 users, started ~08:15 when Okta rotated keys. Org: acme-prod (org_abc123). Urgent please.

alex_support: Sorry to hear that — can you confirm one affected user email and whether this is OIDC or SAML? Any recent config changes on the IdP side?

acme-admin: It's Okta OIDC. Admin rotated signing key and forced session refresh around 08:15. Example affected: lisa@acme.com. Re-login sometimes helps but a subset stays blocked; API calls with the session token return 401/403 intermittently.

alex_support: Got it. Can you try in Incognito to rule out cached cookies and paste (redacted) id_token claims or a screenshot showing the groups/roles claim?

acme-admin: Incognito gives mixed results. Pasting a trimmed id_token claim snippet (redacted):

{
  "sub": "00u1abcd...",
  "email": "lisa@acme.com",
  "groups": "[\"acme-engineering\", \"acme-team-backend\", \"acme-platform-very-long-group-name-truncated\""
}

Notice the groups string is cut off mid-name.

maria_sre: tagging eng-infra @jordan_idp @sam_engineer — this smells like token/cookie truncation. We've hit header/cookie size limits before which silently drop the tail of a claim.

jordan_idp: We pushed a larger groups payload for some customers yesterday (many nested groups). If id_token size makes the session cookie or headers > proxy buffer limit, ingress may truncate. Can someone check the browser network devtools for request headers / cookie size?

acme-admin: Checked devtools: session cookie size ~5120 bytes. Network tab shows 'Request header too large' on some requests right before 403.

sam_engineer: Likely root cause: nginx proxy default buffer sizes ~4k. When the cookie/id_token is cut, our auth middleware sees a malformed/partial groups claim -> role resolution fails -> 403. Short-term: reduce groups in id_token or enable Okta group filters. Longer-term: increase proxy buffer limits or use reference tokens/scoped access tokens.

alex_support: Workarounds we can suggest: 1) Ask Okta admin to filter groups included in id_token (only include assigned groups). 2) Invite affected users as direct collaborators on projects temporarily. Which would you prefer?

acme-admin: We'll have the Okta admin try filtering first. Any immediate test to confirm after they change mapping?

jordan_idp: After mapping change, force a full logout and re-login for the affected users. Then run this check to confirm 'groups' present:

curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <id_token>' https://console.redwood.example.com/api/v1/auth/check

Response should include a non-empty "groups" claim. Also check devtools for cookie length < 4096.

support-bot: Escalation created INC-2026. Assigned to eng-infra: sam_engineer, jordan_idp.

acme-admin: Okta admin enabled group filtering and trimmed a few very long nested group names at 09:40, then did a user resync. Lisa re-logged in and can see project roles again. Confirmed for 8/8 affected users.

alex_support: Great — marking as resolved for now. We'll keep the incident open until eng infra deploys the proxy buffer update. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: Action item: add doc/FAQ entry for "Large id_token / cookie truncation causing 403" with remediation steps (Okta group filters, quick invite workaround, ingress tuning).

acme-admin: Confirmed fixed on our side, thanks for the fast help.

deploy-bot: Note: infra patch to nginx proxy buffer sizes scheduled in rolling window, ETA ~24h.
